objective: Distinguish pollen-dependent resource effects on seed-feeders from true floral-head physical access and independent pollination service

studies.localities: four populations near České Budějovice, Czechia
studies.sexual_state: functionally dioecious, reproductive female plants sampled
studies.unresolved_plant_denominator_discrepancy: Printed 196 biological individuals versus 48 blocks x 4=192 planned slots; no original raw plant CSV inspected

author_reported_outcomes.seed_fraction_predated_under_pollinator_: fraction higher despite fewer emerged arthropods
author_reported_outcomes.predator_exclusion_and_model: no detectable changes reported in major outputs
author_reported_outcomes.sites: effects reported broadly consistent across four populations

studies.insect_taxa: Xyphosia miliaria (tephritid) and its Hymenoptera parasitoids
author_reported_results: Manipulated host-plant resources/quality increased seed-feeder abundance
No evidence that X. miliaria selectively oviposited on nutrient-fertilized plants
Parasitoid attack rates were higher on nutrient-fertilized thistles
studies.term_warning: plant nutrient fertilization in Walker 2008 is NOT the same as pollinator-mediated ovule fertilization in Karpate 2025

comparative_interpretation.source_backed: Pollinator-exclusion, plant nutrients/bud supply, seed-feeder emergence and parasitoids are interconnected in Cirsium experiments.
not_source_backed: Head spines and orientation caused differences in seed-feeder establishment
All emerged insects identified as actual seed consumers
Experimental bag alters only pollen transfer
The two different experiments establish a single same-head mediation coefficient
Any reduction in adult emergence establishes plant adaptive payoff
Karpate preprint outcomes are confirmed peer-reviewed final publication
comparative_interpretation.novel_test_target: Condition on measured resource provisioning and truly independently verified ovipositor access at an authentic bract/spine interface, then compare confirmed eggs/larval survival and absolute filled achenes on the same pre-enrolled biological head
comparative_interpretation.study_unit: individual biological plant, repeated head nested, site and block preserved
